fights.question: It's a tie. Now what?
fights.line: The tied players give one more clue, then everyone revotes between them. Still tied? The imposter wins.
fights.rules: A tie means the group could not agree, so the tied players get one last chance to clear their name before the final vote.
fights.house: Some groups do a straight revote, call it a draw, or give a tie to the imposter straight away.

fights.question: He just said the actual word!
fights.line: The round is cancelled. Deal a new word and nobody scores.
fights.rules: Saying the secret word, a form of it or a translation of it hands the imposter the answer, so the round cannot be played fairly.

fights.question: Can I give my clue in Hindi or Malayalam?
fights.line: Yes, in any language the whole group understands. But the word itself in another language counts as saying the word.
fights.rules: Clues just need to hint at the word. Translating the secret word is the same as saying it.
fights.house: Some groups agree on one language before they start.

fights.question: Can I say I'm the imposter to trick people?
fights.line: You can bluff all you like. Only the card shown at the reveal counts.
fights.rules: Anyone can bluff, ask questions or defend themselves during the talk. A non-imposter who pretends just risks being voted out.

fights.question: Can I pass my turn?
fights.line: No. Everyone must give a clue. If you're stuck, say something vague.
fights.rules: Passing would let the imposter dodge the hardest moment, and it makes a normal player look guilty.

fights.question: Same guy is imposter again, is it rigged?
fights.line: Playref never makes the same person imposter twice in a row, and favours people who have waited longest.
fights.rules: Pure random picking can give streaks, so Playref balances the picks across the night.

fights.question: Does the imposter get a vote?
fights.line: Yes. Everyone votes, the imposter included.
fights.rules: On "3, 2, 1" everyone points at the same moment. The most votes is accused.
fights.house: Some groups vote one by one.

fights.question: Can the imposter guess the word before the vote?
fights.line: Yes, once. They must say "I'm the imposter, the word is ...". Right wins; wrong means they are caught.
fights.rules: An early guess cannot be taken back. With two imposters, a wrong guess catches that one, and the group votes straight away for the other.

fights.question: I forgot the word. Can I look again?
fights.line: Yes. Ask for the phone and peek again on the same hold-to-see screen.
fights.rules: The peek screen looks the same for everyone, so asking for it gives nothing away.

fights.question: One word or a phrase?
fights.line: One word. Some groups allow short phrases of up to 3 words, for kids and grandparents.
fights.rules: One-word clues keep the imposter in the game and the round quick.
fights.house: Short phrases of up to 3 words.

fights.question: We caught one of two imposters. Who wins?
fights.line: The caught one makes a last guess, then you vote once more straight away to find the other. Catch both to win.
fights.rules: With two imposters the group must catch both. Any imposter who escapes or guesses right wins for the imposters.
fights.house: Some groups vote out one player per round until every imposter is out.

fights.question: Can I accuse someone before everyone has given a clue?
fights.line: You can talk any time, but voting only happens after the clue rounds.
fights.rules: Clues first, then open talk, then the vote. Accusing early just gives the imposter more to work with.
